names: Daughter of the Marquis of Jiu

place.en: between the Yellow and Wei rivers

units.zh: 殷契，母曰簡狄，有娀氏之女，為帝嚳次妃。
units.en: Xie of Yin was born to Jiandi, a woman of the Yousong clan and secondary consort of Emperor Ku.
units.literal: Xie of Yin had a mother named Jiandi, of the Yousong clan, who was Di Ku's secondary consort.

units.zh: 三人行浴，見玄鳥墮其卵，簡狄取吞之，因孕生契。
units.en: While Jiandi bathed with two companions, a dark bird dropped an egg; she took it, swallowed it, and conceived Xie.
units.literal: The three of them went to bathe; seeing the dark bird drop its egg, Jiandi took and swallowed it; thereby pregnant she bore Xie.

units.zh: 契長而佐禹治水有功。
units.en: When Xie came of age he helped Yu manage the flood and earned distinction.
units.literal: Xie grew up and assisted Yu in regulating the waters with merit.

units.zh: 帝舜乃命契曰：「百姓不親，五品不訓，汝為司徒而敬敷五教，五教在寬。」
units.en: Emperor Shun appointed Xie and said, "The people are estranged, and the five relationships are not guided. As Minister of Education, spread the five teachings with generous patience."
units.literal: Emperor Shun then charged Xie, saying, "The people lack affection; the five relationships lack instruction. You shall be Minister of Education and reverently spread the five teachings—the five teachings lie in generosity."

units.zh: 封于商，賜姓子氏。
units.en: He received the fief of Shang and the clan name Zi.
units.literal: He was enfeoffed at Shang and granted the surname Zi.

units.zh: 契興於唐、虞、大禹之際，功業著於百姓，百姓以平。
units.en: He rose in the age of Yao, Shun, and Yu the Great; his achievements won renown among the people, and the realm was at peace.
units.literal: He flourished in the time of Yao, Shun, and Great Yu; his deeds won renown among the people and kept the realm at peace.

units.zh: 契卒，子昭明立。
units.en: When Xie died, his son Zhaoming succeeded him.
units.literal: Xie passed away; his son Zhaoming established himself.

units.zh: 昭明卒，子相土立。
units.en: Zhaoming was succeeded by his son Xiang Tu.
units.literal: Zhaoming passed away; his son Xiang Tu established himself.

units.zh: 相土卒，子昌若立。
units.en: Xiang Tu was succeeded by his son Changruo.
units.literal: Xiang Tu passed away; his son Changruo established himself.

units.zh: 昌若卒，子曹圉立。
units.en: Changruo was succeeded by his son Caoyu.
units.literal: Changruo passed away; his son Caoyu established himself.

units.zh: 曹圉卒，子冥立。
units.en: Caoyu was succeeded by his son Ming.
units.literal: Caoyu passed away; his son Ming established himself.

units.zh: 冥卒，子振立。
units.en: Ming was succeeded by his son Zhen.
units.literal: Ming passed away; his son Zhen established himself.

units.zh: 振卒，子微立。
units.en: Zhen was succeeded by his son Wei.
units.literal: Zhen passed away; his son Wei established himself.

units.zh: 微卒，子報丁立。
units.en: Wei was succeeded by his son Baoding.
units.literal: Wei passed away; his son Baoding established himself.

units.zh: 報丁卒，子報乙立。
units.en: Baoding was succeeded by his son Baoyi.
units.literal: Baoding passed away; his son Baoyi established himself.

units.zh: 報乙卒，子報丙立。
units.en: Baoyi was succeeded by his son Baobing.
units.literal: Baoyi passed away; his son Baobing established himself.

units.zh: 報丙卒，子主壬立。
units.en: Baobing was succeeded by his son Zhuren.
units.literal: Baobing passed away; his son Zhuren established himself.

units.zh: 主壬卒，子主癸立。
units.en: Zhuren was succeeded by his son Zhugui.
units.literal: Zhuren passed away; his son Zhugui established himself.

units.zh: 主癸卒，子天乙立，是為成湯。
units.en: Zhugui was succeeded by his son Tianyi—who is known as Cheng Tang.
units.literal: Zhugui passed away; his son Tianyi established himself; this is Cheng Tang.

units.zh: 成湯，自契至湯八遷。
units.en: From Xie to Tang the seat of the line had shifted eight times.
units.literal: Cheng Tang—from Xie to Tang eight migrations.

units.zh: 湯始居亳，從先王居，作帝誥。
units.en: Tang first settled at Bo, beside the tombs of his forebears, and composed the Announcement to Di.
units.literal: Tang first dwelt at Bo, following the residence of the former kings, and composed the Announcement to Di.

units.zh: 湯征諸侯。
units.en: Tang led punitive expeditions against the regional lords.
units.literal: Tang campaigned against the lords.

units.zh: 葛伯不祀，湯始伐之。
units.en: When the lord of Ge failed to perform the sacrifices, Tang attacked him first.
units.literal: Lord of Ge did not sacrifice; Tang first attacked him.

units.zh: 湯曰：「予有言：人視水見形，視民知治不。」
units.en: Tang said, "Men look into water to see their faces; look to the people to know whether rule is sound."
units.literal: Tang said, "I have a saying: people look on water and see form; look on the people and know order or not."

units.zh: 伊尹曰：「明哉！
units.en: Yi Yin replied: "How clear—
units.literal: yiyin said, "How clear!

units.zh: 言能聽，道乃進。
units.en: when counsel is heard, the Way moves forward.
units.literal: When words can be heard, the way then advances.

units.zh: 君國子民，為善者皆在王官。
units.en: The lord who fathers his people gathers every worthy into his court.
units.literal: Ruler of the state, father to the people—all who do good are at the royal court.

units.zh: 勉哉，勉哉！」
units.en: Strive, my lord—never slacken."
units.literal: Exert yourself, exert yourself!"

units.zh: 湯曰：「汝不能敬命，予大罰殛之，無有攸赦。」
units.en: Tang warned, "Whoever spurns my command I will strike down without mercy."
units.literal: Tang said, "You who fail to reverence the command—I will greatly punish and kill you, without any sparing."

units.zh: 作湯征。
units.en: He composed the Tang Punitive Expeditions.
units.literal: He made "Tang's Punitive Expeditions."

units.zh: 伊尹名阿衡。
units.en: Yi Yin was named Aheng.
units.literal: yiyin's name was Aheng.

units.zh: 阿衡欲奸湯而無由，乃為有莘氏媵臣，負鼎俎，以滋味說湯，致于王道。
units.en: Wishing to serve Tang but lacking an introduction, Aheng joined the Youxin bridal procession as a cook, carried pots and boards, won Tang over through his cooking, and drew him toward the kingly Way.
units.literal: Wishing to serve Tang but lacking an introduction, Aheng became a attendant in the Youxin bridal train, carried pots and boards, won Tang over through flavor, and led him toward the kingly Way.

units.zh: 或曰，伊尹處士，湯使人聘迎之，五反然後肯往從湯，言素王及九主之事。
units.en: Others say yiyin was a recluse whom Tang invited five times before he came, then spoke to him of the model rulers and the Nine Masters.
units.literal: Others say yiyin was a recluse whom Tang invited five times before he came, then lectured on the model rulers and the Nine Masters.

units.zh: 湯舉任以國政。
units.en: Tang handed him the administration of the realm.
units.literal: Tang raised and entrusted him with state government.

units.zh: 伊尹去湯適夏。
units.en: yiyin left Tang and went over to the Xia court.
units.literal: yiyin left Tang for Xia.

units.zh: 既醜有夏，復歸于亳。
units.en: Once he had taken Xia's measure, he returned to Bo.
units.literal: Having found fault with You-Xia, he returned to Bo.

units.zh: 入自北門，遇女鳩、女房，作女鳩女房。
units.en: He entered by the north gate, met the ladies Jiuji and Fang, and composed the pieces Nüjiu and Nüfang.
units.literal: Entering by the north gate, he met Nüjiu and Nüfang; he made "Nüjiu and Nüfang."

units.zh: 湯出，見野張網四面，祝曰：「自天下四方皆入吾網。」
units.en: When Tang went abroad, he saw a hunter in the fields who had closed nets on every side, calling, "From all the world and the four quarters let everything come into my net."
units.literal: Tang went out and saw a man in the wilds who had spread nets on all four sides, praying, "From all under Heaven and the four quarters—may all enter my net."

units.zh: 湯曰：「嘻，盡之矣！」
units.en: Tang cried, "No—that would trap every living thing!"
units.literal: Tang said, "Alas—that is utterly too much!"

units.zh: 乃去其三面，祝曰：「欲左，左。
units.en: He had three sides taken down and called out: "If you want left, go left.
units.literal: Thereupon he removed three sides, praying saying, "Want left, left.

units.zh: 欲右，右。
units.en: If you want right, go right.
units.literal: Want right, right.

units.zh: 不用命，乃入吾網。」
units.en: Only those who defy my order need to enter the net."
units.literal: Not obeying command—then enter my net."

units.zh: 諸侯聞之，曰：「湯德至矣，及禽獸。」
units.en: When the feudal lords heard of this, they said, "Tang’s virtue has reached its height; it extends even to birds and beasts."
units.literal: When the lords heard of it, they said, "Tang's virtue has reached such a point that it extends even to birds and beasts."

units.zh: 當是時，夏桀為虐政淫荒，而諸侯昆吾氏為亂。
units.en: At this time Jie of Xia governed with cruelty and excess, and the lords of Kunwu raised disorder.
units.literal: In those days Jie of Xia ruled with cruelty and excess while the Kunwu lords stirred rebellion.

units.zh: 湯乃興師率諸侯，伊尹從湯，湯自把鉞以伐昆吾，遂伐桀。
units.en: Tang then raised an army of the lords, yiyin at his side, and himself wielded the axe against Kunwu before marching on Jie.
units.literal: Tang thereupon raised troops leading the lords; yiyin followed Tang; Tang himself grasped the battle-axe to attack Kunwu, then attacked Jie.

units.zh: 湯曰：「格女眾庶，來，女悉聽朕言。
units.en: Tang addressed the host: "Come, all of you, and hear my words.
units.literal: Tang said, "Come you multitude, come, you all listen to my words.

units.zh: 匪台小子敢行舉亂，有夏多罪，予維聞女眾言，夏氏有罪。
units.en: It is not I who dare stir revolt; Xia is heavy with crime—I have heard you yourselves say the Xia house is guilty.
units.literal: It is not I, the little child, who dare raise disorder; You-Xia has many crimes—I only have heard you multitudes speak—the Xia clan has guilt.

units.zh: 予畏上帝，不敢不正。
units.en: I fear Heaven and dare not withhold punishment.
units.literal: I fear Supreme God; I dare not fail to correct.

units.zh: 今夏多罪，天命殛之。
units.en: Xia's crimes are many; Heaven has ordered its destruction.
units.literal: Now Xia has many crimes; Heaven's mandate is to strike it dead.

units.zh: 今女有眾，女曰：『我君不恤我眾，捨我嗇事而割政』。
units.en: You say among yourselves: Our king does not pity us—he sets aside our field work and meddles with government.
units.literal: Now you have a multitude; you say, 'Our lord does not pity us multitudes, casts aside our harvest toil and cuts policy.

units.zh: 女其曰：『有罪，其柰何』？
units.en: You ask: If there is fault, what can be done?
units.literal: You will say, 'If there is guilt, what then shall be done?

units.zh: 夏王率止眾力，率奪夏國。
units.en: The king of Xia has drained your strength and plundered the Xia domain.
units.literal: The Xia king has led astray and exhausted the multitude's strength, led and seized the Xia state.

units.zh: 有眾率怠不和，曰：『是日何時喪？
units.en: The people have grown slack and bitter, crying: "When will this sun set?
units.literal: The multitude has led slackness and discord, saying, 'When will this sun perish?

units.zh: 予與女皆亡』！
units.en: I will perish with you!"
units.literal: I and you will all perish!

units.zh: 夏德若茲，今朕必往。
units.en: Xia's conduct is such that I must march against it.
units.literal: Xia's virtue being thus, now I must go.

units.zh: 爾尚及予一人致天之罰，予其大理女。
units.en: Join me, the One Man, in carrying out Heaven's sentence, and I will reward you richly.
units.literal: You still may join me, the One Man, to inflict Heaven's punishment—I will greatly order you.

units.zh: 女毋不信，朕不食言。
units.en: Do not doubt me—I keep my oath.
units.literal: You must not disbelieve—I do not break my word.

units.zh: 女不從誓言，予則帑僇女，無有攸赦。」
units.en: Whoever breaks this oath I will execute, you and your families, without mercy."
units.literal: You who do not follow the sworn words—I will put you and your kin to death, without any sparing."

units.zh: 以告令師，作湯誓。
units.en: He proclaimed this to the host and composed the Oath of Tang.
units.literal: He reported this to the army and composed the Oath of Tang.

units.zh: 於是湯曰：「吾甚武」，號曰武王。
units.en: Tang then said, "I am greatly martial," and took the title Martial King.
units.literal: Thereupon Tang said, "I am very martial," and styled himself Martial King.

units.zh: 桀敗於有娀之虛，桀奔於鳴條，夏師敗績。
units.en: Jie was beaten at Yousong, fled to Mingtiao, and his army was routed.
units.literal: Jie was defeated at the ruins of Yousong; Jie fled to Mingtiao; Xia's army suffered rout.

units.zh: 湯遂伐三嵕，俘厥寶玉，義伯、仲伯作典寶。
units.en: Tang then attacked Sanzong, seized its sacred jades, and the lords Yibo and Zhongbo composed the Canon of the Treasure.
units.literal: Tang then attacked Sanzong, seized its sacred jades, and Yibo and Zhongbo composed the Canon of the Treasure.

units.zh: 湯既勝夏，欲遷其社，不可，作夏社。
units.en: After conquering Xia, Tang wished to relocate its soil altar but could not, and composed Xia's Earth Altar.
units.literal: Tang having conquered Xia, wished to move its earth altar, could not, and made "Xia's Earth Altar."

units.zh: 伊尹報。
units.en: yiyin made his report.
units.literal: yiyin presented his report.

units.zh: 於是諸侯畢服，湯乃踐天子位，平定海內。
units.en: The lords all submitted; Tang took the throne and brought peace within the seas.
units.literal: The lords all submitted; Tang took the throne and brought peace inside the seas.

units.zh: 湯歸至于泰卷陶，中壘作誥。
units.en: On his return Tang halted at Taijuan Tao, where Zhonglei composed the proclamations.
units.literal: On his return Tang halted at Taijuan Tao, where Zhonglei composed the announcements.

units.zh: 既絀夏命，還亳，作湯誥：「維三月，王自至於東郊。
units.en: After ending Xia's mandate he returned to Bo and issued Tang's Announcement: "In the third month the king came in person to the eastern suburbs.
units.literal: Having ended Xia's mandate, he returned to Bo and made "Tang's Announcement": "It is the third month; the king personally reached the eastern suburbs.

units.zh: 告諸侯群后：『毋不有功於民，勤力乃事。
units.en: He told the assembled rulers: None of you may neglect the people; labor diligently at your duties.
units.literal: He told the lords and host of rulers: 'None shall fail to work for the people; exert yourselves in your tasks.

units.zh: 予乃大罰殛女，毋予怨。』
units.en: Or I will punish you severely—do not blame me for it.
units.literal: I will then greatly punish and kill you—do not blame me.

units.zh: 曰：『古禹、皋陶久勞于外，其有功乎民，民乃有安。
units.en: He said: Long ago Yu and Gao Yao worked far from court; they served the people, and the people found peace.
units.literal: Saying: 'Of old Yu and Gao Yao long toiled outside; they had merit toward the people; the people then had rest.

units.zh: 東為江，北為濟，西為河，南為淮，四瀆已修，萬民乃有居。
units.en: East lay the Long River, north the Ji, west the Yellow River, south the Huai—the four streams were tamed, and the people had homes.
units.literal: East was the Yangtze, north was the Ji, west was the He, south was the Huai—the four channels were repaired; the myriad people then had dwellings.

units.zh: 后稷降播，農殖百穀。
units.en: Hou Ji brought down seed and taught farming of every grain.
units.literal: Prince Millet descended and sowed, farming planted the hundred grains.

units.zh: 三公咸有功于民，故後有立。
units.en: The three high ministers all served the people, and their lines were founded in turn.
units.literal: The three dukes all had merit toward the people; therefore afterward they had establishment.

units.zh: 昔蚩尤與其大夫作亂百姓，帝乃弗予，有狀。
units.en: When Chiyou and his officers ravaged the people, Heaven withdrew favor—there was clear cause.
units.literal: Of old Chiyou with his great officers made disorder among the hundred surnames; the Emperor then did not grant him—there was evidence.

units.zh: 先王言不可不勉。』
units.en: The words of the former kings must be heeded.
units.literal: The former kings' words must not go unheeded.

units.zh: 曰：『不道，毋之在國，女毋我怨。』」
units.en: He added: If you stray from the Way, you shall not remain in power—do not resent me for it."
units.literal: Saying: 'If not the Way, do not let it remain in the state—you must not resent me.'

units.zh: 以令諸侯。
units.en: Thus, he charged the regional lords.
units.literal: Thereby commanding the lords.

units.zh: 伊尹作咸有一德，咎單作明居。
units.en: Yi Yin composed All Possess One Virtue, and Jiu Dan composed Bright Dwelling.
units.literal: yiyin composed All Possess One Virtue; Jiusdan composed Bright Dwelling.

units.zh: 湯乃改正朔，易服色，上白，朝會以晝。
units.en: Tang then changed the calendar, altered the color of court dress to honor white, and held audiences in daylight.
units.literal: Tang reformed the calendar, changed the court dress to favor white, and held audiences by day.

units.zh: 湯崩，太子太丁未立而卒，於是乃立太丁之弟外丙，是為帝外丙。
units.en: When Tang died, the heir Taiding died before he could rule, so Taiding's brother Waibing became Emperor Waibing.
units.literal: Tang passed away; heir son Taiding had not been established then died; thereupon they established Taiding's younger brother Waibing—this is Emperor Waibing.

units.zh: 帝外丙即位三年，崩，立外丙之弟中壬，是為帝中壬。
units.en: Waibing ruled three years and died; his brother Zhongren succeeded as Emperor Zhongren.
units.literal: Emperor Waibing having assumed position three years, passed away; they established Waibing's younger brother Zhongren—this is Emperor Zhongren.

units.zh: 帝中壬即位四年，崩，伊尹乃立太丁之子太甲。
units.en: Zhongren ruled four years and died; yiyin then set Taiding's son Taijia on the throne.
units.literal: Emperor Zhongren having assumed position four years, passed away; yiyin then established Taiding's son Taijia.

units.zh: 太甲，成湯適長孫也，是為帝太甲。
units.en: Taijia was Cheng Tang's senior great-grandson through the main line—Emperor Taijia.
units.literal: Taijia, Cheng Tang's eldest great-grandson by the proper line—this is Emperor Taijia.

units.zh: 帝太甲元年，伊尹作伊訓，作肆命，作徂后。
units.en: In Emperor Taijia’s first year, Yi Yin composed the Instructions for Taijia, the Broad Commands, and The Departed Sovereign.
units.literal: In Taijia's first year yiyin composed the Instructions for Taijia, the Loose Commands, and Gone Kings.

units.zh: 帝太甲既立三年，不明，暴虐，不遵湯法，亂德，於是伊尹放之於桐宮。
units.en: After three years Taijia proved dark, violent, and lawless; yiyin banished him to the Tong palace.
units.literal: Emperor Taijia having been established three years, was not enlightened, cruel and tyrannical, did not follow Tang's laws, disordered virtue; thereupon yiyin banished him to Tong Palace.

units.zh: 三年，伊尹攝行政當國，以朝諸侯。
units.en: For three years yiyin ruled as regent and received the lords at court.
units.literal: Three years yiyin exercised government in proxy and held court over the lords.

units.zh: 帝太甲居桐宮三年，悔過自責，反善，於是伊尹乃迎帝太甲而授之政。
units.en: Taijia spent three years in Tong, repented, and mended his ways; yiyin then brought him back and restored the government.
units.literal: Emperor Taijia dwelling in Tong Palace three years, repented fault and blamed himself, returned to good; thereupon yiyin then welcomed Emperor Taijia and handed him the government.

units.zh: 帝太甲修德，諸侯咸歸殷，百姓以寧。
units.en: Taijia cultivated virtue; the lords rallied to Yin again and the people were calmed.
units.literal: Emperor Taijia cultivated virtue; the lords all returned to Yin; the hundred surnames thereby were tranquil.

units.zh: 伊尹嘉之，乃作太甲訓三篇，褒帝太甲，稱太宗。
units.en: yiyin praised him, composed the three Instructions of Taijia, and honored him as Grand Ancestor.
units.literal: yiyin praised him, composed the three Instructions of Taijia, honored him as Grand Ancestor.

units.zh: 太宗崩，子沃丁立。
units.en: When the Grand Ancestor died, his son Woding succeeded.
units.literal: Grand Ancestor passed away; his son Woding established himself.

units.zh: 帝沃丁之時，伊尹卒。
units.en: Under Woding, yiyin died.
units.literal: In Emperor Woding's time, yiyin passed away.

units.zh: 既葬伊尹於亳，咎單遂訓伊尹事，作沃丁。
units.en: After Yi Yin had been buried at Bo, Jiu Dan set forth Yi Yin’s deeds in instruction and composed Woding.
units.literal: After yiyin was buried at Bo, Jiusdan expounded his deeds in the piece called Woding.

units.zh: 沃丁崩，弟太庚立，是為帝太庚。
units.en: Woding died; his brother Taigeng became Emperor Taigeng.
units.literal: Woding passed away; younger brother Taigeng established himself—this is Emperor Taigeng.

units.zh: 帝太庚崩，子帝小甲立。
units.en: Taigeng died and his son Xiaojia ruled.
units.literal: Emperor Taigeng passed away; his son Emperor Xiaojia established himself.

units.zh: 帝小甲崩，弟雍己立，是為帝雍己。
units.en: Xiaojia died; his brother Yongji became Emperor Yongji.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaojia passed away; younger brother Yongji established himself—this is Emperor Yongji.

units.zh: 殷道衰，諸侯或不至。
units.en: Yin's power waned, and some lords stayed away from court.
units.literal: Yin's way declined; some lords did not come to court.

units.zh: 帝雍己崩，弟太戊立，是為帝太戊。
units.en: Yongji died; his brother Taiwu became Emperor Taiwu.
units.literal: Emperor Yongji passed away; younger brother Taiwu established himself—this is Emperor Taiwu.

units.zh: 帝太戊立伊陟為相。
units.en: Taiwu appointed Yizhi chief minister.
units.literal: Emperor Taiwu established Yizhi as minister.

units.zh: 亳有祥桑谷共生於朝，一暮大拱。
units.en: At Bo mulberry and grain sprouted together in the courtyard and in one night grew thick as an arm.
units.literal: At Bo there was an omen: mulberry and grain grew together in the court; in one night they became as thick as a clasped hand.

units.zh: 帝太戊懼，問伊陟。
units.en: Taiwu was frightened and asked Yizhi what it meant.
units.literal: Emperor Taiwu feared and questioned Yizhi.

units.zh: 伊陟曰：「臣聞妖不勝德，帝之政其有闕與？
units.en: Yizhi said, "I have heard that portents cannot overcome virtue. Perhaps there is a flaw in your government?
units.literal: Yizhi said, "I have heard that portents cannot overcome virtue—perhaps there is a flaw in your government?

units.zh: 帝其修德。」
units.en: My lord, cultivate your virtue."
units.literal: The king must cultivate his virtue."

units.zh: 太戊從之，而祥桑枯死而去。
units.en: Taiwu listened; the strange mulberry died away.
units.literal: Taiwu followed it, and the auspicious mulberry withered and departed.

units.zh: 伊陟贊言于巫咸。
units.en: Yizhi relayed this counsel to Wuxian.
units.literal: Yizhi praised the words to Wuxian.

units.zh: 巫咸治王家有成，作咸艾，作太戊。
units.en: Wu Xian brought order to the royal house and achieved success; he composed Xian Ai and Taiwu.
units.literal: Wuxian brought order to the royal house and composed Xian Ai and Taiwu.

units.zh: 帝太戊贊伊陟于廟，言弗臣，伊陟讓，作原命。
units.en: Emperor Taiwu praised Yi Zhi in the ancestral temple, speaking of him as more than a mere minister. Yi Zhi declined the honor, and Original Mandate was composed.
units.literal: Taiwu honored Yizhi in the temple as more than a mere minister; Yizhi declined, and the Original Mandate was composed.

units.zh: 殷復興，諸侯歸之，故稱中宗。
units.en: Yin flourished again and the lords rallied—hence he is called the Middle Ancestor.
units.literal: Yin revived; the lords returned to it; therefore he is called Middle Ancestor.

units.zh: 中宗崩，子帝中丁立。
units.en: When the Middle Ancestor died, his son Zhongding succeeded.
units.literal: Middle Ancestor passed away; his son Emperor Zhongding established himself.

units.zh: 帝中丁遷于隞。
units.en: Zhongding moved the capital to Ao.
units.literal: Emperor Zhongding moved the capital to Ao.

units.zh: 河亶甲居相。
units.en: Hedanjia ruled from Xiang.
units.literal: Hedanjia dwelt at Xiang.

units.zh: 祖乙遷于邢。
units.en: Zuyi moved the seat to Xing.
units.literal: Zuyi moved the capital to Xing.

units.zh: 帝中丁崩，弟外壬立，是為帝外壬。
units.en: Zhongding died; his brother Wairen became Emperor Wairen.
units.literal: Emperor Zhongding passed away; younger brother Wairen established himself—this is Emperor Wairen.

units.zh: 仲丁書闕不具。
units.en: The written records for Zhongding are missing and incomplete.
units.literal: The records of Zhongding are lost and incomplete.

units.zh: 帝外壬崩，弟河亶甲立，是為帝河亶甲。
units.en: Wairen died; his brother Hedanjia became Emperor Hedanjia.
units.literal: Emperor Wairen passed away; younger brother Hedanjia established himself—this is Emperor Hedanjia.

units.zh: 河亶甲時，殷復衰。
units.en: Under Hedanjia Yin weakened again.
units.literal: In Hedanjia's time, Yin again declined.

units.zh: 河亶甲崩，子帝祖乙立。
units.en: Hedanjia died and his son Zuyi ruled.
units.literal: Hedanjia passed away; his son Emperor Zuyi established himself.

units.zh: 帝祖乙立，殷復興。
units.en: When Zuyi came to the throne, Yin revived once more.
units.literal: Emperor Zuyi having been established, Yin again revived.

units.zh: 巫賢任職。
units.en: Wuxian the shaman served in office.
units.literal: Wuxian held office.

units.zh: 祖乙崩，子帝祖辛立。
units.en: Zuyi died and his son Zuxin ruled.
units.literal: Zuyi passed away; his son Emperor Zuxin established himself.

units.zh: 帝祖辛崩，弟沃甲立，是為帝沃甲。
units.en: Zuxin died; his brother Wojia became Emperor Wojia.
units.literal: Emperor Zuxin passed away; younger brother Wojia established himself—this is Emperor Wojia.

units.zh: 帝沃甲崩，立沃甲兄祖辛之子祖丁，是為帝祖丁。
units.en: Wojia died; Zuxin's son Zuding, Wojia's nephew, became Emperor Zuding.
units.literal: Emperor Wojia passed away; they established Wojia's elder brother Zuxin's son Zuding—this is Emperor Zuding.

units.zh: 帝祖丁崩，立弟沃甲之子南庚，是為帝南庚。
units.en: Zuding died; Wojia's son Nangeng succeeded as Emperor Nangeng.
units.literal: Emperor Zuding passed away; they established younger brother Wojia's son Nangeng—this is Emperor Nangeng.

units.zh: 帝南庚崩，立帝祖丁之子陽甲，是為帝陽甲。
units.en: Nangeng died; Zuding's son Yangjia became Emperor Yangjia.
units.literal: Emperor Nangeng passed away; they established Emperor Zuding's son Yangjia—this is Emperor Yangjia.

units.zh: 帝陽甲之時，殷衰。
units.en: Under Yangjia Yin declined again.
units.literal: In Emperor Yangjia's time, Yin declined.

units.zh: 自中丁以來，廢適而更立諸弟子，弟子或爭相代立，比九世亂，於是諸侯莫朝。
units.en: From Zhongding on, the rightful heir was set aside for younger brothers, who fought for the throne. Nine reigns ran into chaos, and the lords ceased to attend court.
units.literal: From Zhongding on the rightful heir was set aside for younger brothers, who fought for the throne—nine reigns of chaos—and the lords ceased to attend court.

units.zh: 帝陽甲崩，弟盤庚立，是為帝盤庚。
units.en: Yangjia died; his brother Pangeng became Emperor Pangeng.
units.literal: Emperor Yangjia passed away; younger brother Pangeng established himself—this is Emperor Pangeng.

units.zh: 帝盤庚之時，殷已都河北，盤庚渡河南，復居成湯之故居，乃五遷，無定處。
units.en: Yin had already sat north of the Yellow River; Pangeng crossed south to Cheng Tang's old capital. In all, there were five moves, and the court never stayed long in one place.
units.literal: Yin had already sat north of the Yellow River; Pangeng crossed south to Cheng Tang's old capital—five moves in all, never long in one place.

units.zh: 殷民咨胥皆怨，不欲徙。
units.en: The people of Yin grumbled and refused to move.
units.literal: Yin people consulted and murmured all resentful, not wishing to move.

units.zh: 盤庚乃告諭諸侯大臣曰：「昔高后成湯與爾之先祖俱定天下，法則可修。
units.en: Pangeng addressed the lords and ministers: "Long ago High Tang and your forebears founded the realm together; its laws can still be honored.
units.literal: Pangeng addressed the lords and ministers: Long ago High Tang and your forebears founded the realm together—its laws can still be honored.

units.zh: 舍而弗勉，何以成德！」
units.en: If you cast them aside and slacken, how will virtue be perfected?"
units.literal: If you cast them aside and fail to exert yourselves, how can you complete your virtue?"

units.zh: 乃遂涉河南，治亳，行湯之政，然後百姓由寧，殷道復興。
units.en: He crossed the river, ruled from Bo, restored Tang's policies, and the people found rest as Yin rose again.
units.literal: Thereupon he crossed south of the He, governed Bo, practiced Tang's government; then the hundred surnames thereby were tranquil; Yin's way again revived.

units.zh: 諸侯來朝，以其遵成湯之德也。
units.en: The lords returned to court because he followed Tang's example.
units.literal: The lords came to court, because they followed Cheng Tang's virtue.

units.zh: 帝盤庚崩，弟小辛立，是為帝小辛。
units.en: Pangeng died; his brother Xiaoxin became Emperor Xiaoxin.
units.literal: Emperor Pangeng passed away; younger brother Xiaoxin established himself—this is Emperor Xiaoxin.

units.zh: 帝小辛立，殷復衰。
units.en: Under Xiaoxin Yin weakened again.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaoxin having been established, Yin again declined.

units.zh: 百姓思盤庚，乃作盤庚三篇。
units.en: The people longed for Pangeng, and the three chapters of Pangeng were composed.
units.literal: The hundred surnames longed for Pangeng; thereupon the three chapters of Pangeng were composed.

units.zh: 帝小辛崩，弟小乙立，是為帝小乙。
units.en: Xiaoxin died; his brother Xiaoyi succeeded.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaoxin passed away; younger brother Xiaoyi established himself—this is Emperor Xiaoyi.

units.zh: 帝小乙崩，子帝武丁立。
units.en: Xiaoyi died and his son Wuding ruled.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaoyi passed away; his son Emperor Wuding established himself.

units.zh: 帝武丁即位，思復興殷，而未得其佐。
units.en: Wuding wished to restore Yin but had not yet found the right minister.
units.literal: Emperor Wuding having assumed the throne, thought to revive Yin but had not yet found his helper.

units.zh: 三年不言，政事決定於冢宰，以觀國風。
units.en: For three years he held his tongue while the chief minister decided affairs, the better to read the realm.
units.literal: For three years he did not speak; government was decided by the chief minister, to observe the customs of the state.

units.zh: 武丁夜夢得聖人，名曰說。
units.en: One night Wuding dreamed of a sage named Yue.
units.literal: Wuding night dreamed he obtained a sage, named Yue.

units.zh: 以夢所見視群臣百吏，皆非也。
units.en: He compared the vision to his officers—none fit the dream.
units.literal: According to the dream's appearance he viewed ministers and hundred clerks—none matched.

units.zh: 於是乃使百工營求之野，得說於傅險中。
units.en: He sent artisans to search the wilds and found Yue at Fu ravine.
units.literal: Thereupon he sent craftsmen to seek in the wilds and obtained Yue at Fu ravine.

units.zh: 是時說為胥靡，筑於傅險。
units.en: At that time Yue was a corvée laborer, building at Fu ravine.
units.literal: At that time Yue was a convict laborer, building at Fu ravine.

units.zh: 見於武丁，武丁曰是也。
units.en: When he was brought to Wuding, the king said, This is the man.
units.literal: Presented to Wuding, Wuding said this is he.

units.zh: 得而與之語，果聖人，舉以為相，殷國大治。
units.en: They spoke and found him a sage; he was made minister and Yin was well governed.
units.literal: Having obtained him and conversed with him, he was indeed a sage; raised to be minister—Yin state was greatly ordered.

units.zh: 故遂以傅險姓之，號曰傅說。
units.en: He took his name from Fu ravine and was called Fu Yue.
units.literal: Therefore, they took Fu ravine as his surname, styled Fu Yue.

units.zh: 帝武丁祭成湯，明日，有飛雉登鼎耳而呴，武丁懼。
units.en: Wuding sacrificed to Tang; the next day a pheasant lit on the cauldron's ear and cried; the king was afraid.
units.literal: Emperor Wuding sacrificed to Cheng Tang; next day a flying pheasant perched on the tripod ear and crowed; Wuding feared.

units.zh: 祖己曰：「王勿憂，先修政事。」
units.en: Zuji said, "Do not fear, my king. Set your government in order first."
units.literal: Zuji said, "Do not fear, my king—set your government in order first."

units.zh: 祖己乃訓王曰：「唯天監下典厥義，降年有永有不永，非天夭民，中絕其命。
units.en: Zuji lectured the king: "Heaven looks down and grounds its justice in right conduct; it grants long or short life, not to cut men off in youth but to end those who stray mid-course.
units.literal: Zuji lectured the king: Heaven looks down and grounds its justice in right conduct; it grants long or short life—not to cut men off in youth but to end those who stray mid-course.

units.zh: 民有不若德，不聽罪，天既附命正厥德，乃曰其奈何。
units.en: When men lack fitting virtue and ignore their faults, Heaven attaches a charge to straighten their conduct—then we ask what is to be done.
units.literal: When the people lack virtue fitting them, refuse to hear their guilt, Heaven having attached mandate corrects their virtue—then it says what can be done.

units.zh: 鳴呼！
units.en: Alas!
units.literal: Alas!

units.zh: 王嗣敬民，罔非天繼，常祀毋禮于棄道。」
units.en: The king's heir must honor the people. All live under Heaven's succession; in your regular rites never carelessly abandon the Way."
units.literal: The king's heir must honor the people—all live under Heaven's succession; in your regular rites never carelessly abandon the Way."

units.zh: 武丁修政行德，天下咸驩，殷道復興。
units.en: Wuding set his house in order and practiced virtue; the realm rejoiced and Yin flourished again.
units.literal: Wuding cultivated government and practiced virtue; all under Heaven rejoiced; Yin's way again revived.

units.zh: 帝武丁崩，子帝祖庚立。
units.en: Wuding died and his son Zugeng succeeded.
units.literal: Emperor Wuding passed away; his son Emperor Zugeng established himself.

units.zh: 祖己嘉武丁之以祥雉為德，立其廟為高宗，遂作高宗肜日及訓。
units.en: Zu Ji praised Wu Ding for turning the auspicious pheasant omen into virtue; his temple was established as Gaozong, and Gaozong’s Rong Day and its instruction were composed.
units.literal: Zuji praised Wuding for turning the pheasant omen to good; his temple was titled Gaozong, and the Congratulatory Day of Gaozong and related texts were composed.

units.zh: 帝祖庚崩，弟祖甲立，是為帝甲。
units.en: Zugeng died; his brother Zujia became Emperor Jia.
units.literal: Emperor Zugeng passed away; younger brother Zujia established himself—this is Emperor Jia.

units.zh: 帝甲淫亂，殷復衰。
units.en: Emperor Jia gave himself to vice and Yin declined again.
units.literal: Emperor Jia dissolute and chaotic, Yin again declined.

units.zh: 帝甲崩，子帝廩辛立。
units.en: Jia died and his son Linxin ruled.
units.literal: Emperor Jia passed away; his son Emperor Linxin established himself.

units.zh: 帝廩辛崩，弟庚丁立，是為帝庚丁。
units.en: Linxin died; his brother Gengding succeeded.
units.literal: Emperor Linxin passed away; younger brother Gengding established himself—this is Emperor Gengding.

units.zh: 帝庚丁崩，子帝武乙立。
units.en: Gengding died and his son Wuyi ruled.
units.literal: Emperor Gengding passed away; his son Emperor Wuyi established himself.

units.zh: 殷復去亳，徙河北。
units.en: Yin again abandoned Bo and moved north of the Yellow River.
units.literal: Yin again left Bo, moved north of the He.

units.zh: 帝武乙無道，為偶人，謂之天神。
units.en: Emperor Wu Yi was without the Way: he made a puppet and called it the god of Heaven.
units.literal: Wuyi was lawless: he fashioned a straw figure and called it the god of Heaven.

units.zh: 與之博，令人為行。
units.en: He played dice against it while others moved the pieces.
units.literal: He gambled with it, having men act the moves.

units.zh: 天神不勝，乃僇辱之。
units.en: When the dummy lost, he had it mocked and disgraced.
units.literal: When Heaven's Spirit did not win, he then humiliated and shamed it.

units.zh: 為革囊，盛血，卬而射之，命曰「射天」。
units.en: He filled a leather sack with blood, hung it up, shot it, and called the game "shooting Heaven."
units.literal: He made a leather bag, filled it with blood, raised and shot it, naming it "shooting Heaven."

units.zh: 武乙獵於河渭之閒，暴雷，武乙震死。
units.en: Wuyi hunted between the Yellow and Wei rivers; a thunderbolt struck and killed him.
units.literal: Wuyi hunted between the He and Wei; violent thunder struck; Wuyi was killed by lightning.

units.zh: 子帝太丁立。
units.en: His son Taiding succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Emperor Taiding established himself.

units.zh: 帝太丁崩，子帝乙立。
units.en: Taiding died and his son Yi ruled.
units.literal: Emperor Taiding passed away; his son Emperor Yi established himself.

units.zh: 帝乙立，殷益衰。
units.en: Under Emperor Yi, Yin declined further.
units.literal: When Emperor Yi came to the throne, Yin declined further.

units.zh: 帝乙長子曰微子啟，啟母賤，不得嗣。
units.en: Yi's eldest son was Weizi Qi, but Qi's mother was of low rank so he could not inherit.
units.literal: Emperor Yi's eldest son was Weizi Qi; Qi's mother was lowly—he could not succeed.

units.zh: 少子辛，辛母正后，辛為嗣。
units.en: The younger son Xin had a queen mother and became heir.
units.literal: Younger son Xin; Xin's mother was the proper queen—Xin was heir.

units.zh: 帝乙崩，子辛立，是為帝辛，天下謂之紂。
units.en: When Yi died, Xin ruled as Emperor Xin, the man the world calls Zhou.
units.literal: When Yi died, Xin ruled as Emperor Xin—the man the world calls Zhou.

units.zh: 帝紂資辨捷疾，聞見甚敏；
units.en: Zhou was quick-witted and sharp of hearing and sight;
units.literal: King Zhou was clever, eloquent, and quick of hearing and sight;

units.zh: 材力過人，手格猛獸；
units.en: his strength exceeded that of other men, and he could wrestle wild beasts with his bare hands;
units.literal: his strength surpassed others, his hands could grapple fierce beasts;

units.zh: 知足以距諫，言足以飾非；
units.en: his wits let him brush off advice and his tongue varnish any fault;
units.literal: his knowledge enough to reject remonstrance, his words enough to gloss fault;

units.zh: 矜人臣以能，高天下以聲，以為皆出己之下。
units.en: he flaunted his talents to his ministers, looked down on the realm, and fancied none his equal.
units.literal: he boasted to ministers of his ability, raised himself above the realm in reputation, thinking all came out below himself.

units.zh: 好酒淫樂，嬖於婦人。
units.en: He drowned in wine and lewd music and doted on women.
units.literal: He loved wine and dissolute music, doted on women.

units.zh: 愛妲己，妲己之言是從。
units.en: He adored Daji and obeyed her every word.
units.literal: He loved Daji; whatever Daji said he followed.

units.zh: 於是使師涓作新淫聲，北里之舞，靡靡之樂。
units.en: He had Master Juan compose decadent airs, dances of the northern lanes, and enervating tunes.
units.literal: Thereupon he had Master Juan make new licentious sounds, northern quarter dances, dissolving music.

units.zh: 厚賦稅以實鹿臺之錢，而盈鉅橋之粟。
units.en: He piled taxes to stock Lutai with gold and Juliao with grain.
units.literal: He increased taxes to fill Lutai's coin and overflow Juliao's grain.

units.zh: 益收狗馬奇物，充仞宮室。
units.en: He gathered dogs, horses, and rarities until the palaces burst.
units.literal: He further gathered dogs, horses, and curiosities, filling the palace chambers.

units.zh: 益廣沙丘苑臺，多取野獸蜚鳥置其中。
units.en: He widened the Shaqiu hunting park and tower and filled them with beasts and birds.
units.literal: He further enlarged the Shaqiu park and tower, taking many wild beasts and flying birds to place within.

units.zh: 慢於鬼神。
units.en: He neglected the ghosts and spirits.
units.literal: He was negligent toward ghosts and spirits.

units.zh: 大聚樂戲於沙丘，以酒為池，縣肉為林，使男女裸相逐其閒，為長夜之飲。
units.en: He staged revels at Shaqiu with a lake of wine, a forest of hanging meat, naked men and women sporting between them, and feasts that lasted the night through.
units.literal: He greatly gathered music and games at Shaqiu, made a pool of wine, hung meat as a forest, had men and women chase each other naked among them, drinking the long night.

units.zh: 百姓怨望而諸侯有畔者，於是紂乃重刑辟，有炮格之法。
units.en: The people muttered and lords rebelled; Zhou answered with crueller laws and the heated-pillar torture.
units.literal: The people muttered and lords rebelled; Zhou answered with crueler laws and the heated-pillar torture.

units.zh: 以西伯昌、九侯、鄂侯為三公。
units.en: He named Western Earl Chang, the Marquis of Jiu, and the Marquis of E as the three high dukes.
units.literal: He made Western Earl Chang, the Nine Marquises, and the Marquis of E the three dukes.

units.zh: 九侯有好女，入之紂。
units.en: The Nine Marquises offered a beautiful daughter to the court.
units.literal: The Nine Marquises had a beautiful daughter; she was sent in to Zhou.

units.zh: 九侯女不喜淫，紂怒，殺之，而醢九侯。
units.en: She disliked debauchery; Zhou killed her in fury and had the Nine Marquises ground to paste.
units.literal: The Nine Marquises' daughter did not love dissipation; Zhou in anger killed her and minced the Nine Marquises.

units.zh: 鄂侯爭之彊，辨之疾，并脯鄂侯。
units.en: The Marquis of E remonstrated fiercely; Zhou had him pickled as well.
units.literal: The Marquis of E disputed it strongly and argued it swiftly; Zhou also pickled the Marquis of E.

units.zh: 西伯昌聞之，竊嘆。
units.en: When Western Earl Chang heard this, he privately sighed.
units.literal: When Western Earl Chang heard this he sighed in private.

units.zh: 崇侯虎知之，以告紂，紂囚西伯羑里。
units.en: Chonghou Hu informed on him, and Zhou jailed the Western Earl at Youli.
units.literal: Chonghou Hu knew it, reported to Zhou; Zhou imprisoned Western Earl at Youli.

units.zh: 西伯之臣閎夭之徒，求美女奇物善馬以獻紂，紂乃赦西伯。
units.en: His men Hongyao and the rest ransomed him with beauties, treasures, and horses, and Zhou set him free.
units.literal: Western Earl's ministers Hongyao and others sought beauties, curiosities, and fine horses to present to Zhou; Zhou then pardoned Western Earl.

units.zh: 西伯出而獻洛西之地，以請除炮格之刑。
units.en: On his release he ceded the lands west of the Luo to buy the abolition of the heated-pillar torture.
units.literal: Western Earl coming out presented the lands west of the Luo, requesting removal of the heated-pillar punishment.

units.zh: 紂乃許之，賜弓矢斧鉞，使得征伐，為西伯。
units.en: Zhou agreed and gave him bow, axe, and halberd with authority to wage war as Western Earl.
units.literal: Zhou then granted it, gave bow, arrows, axe, and halberd, allowing him to campaign, making him Western Earl.

units.zh: 而用費中為政。
units.en: Yet he put Fei Zhong in charge of government.
units.literal: Yet he employed Fei Zhong to govern.

units.zh: 費中善諛，好利，殷人弗親。
units.en: Fei Zhong flattered and grasped after gain; the Yin people did not trust him.
units.literal: Fei Zhong was skilled at flattery, loved profit—Yin people did not cleave to him.

units.zh: 紂又用惡來。
units.en: Zhou also employed E Lai.
units.literal: Zhou again employed E Lai.

units.zh: 惡來善毀讒，諸侯以此益疏。
units.en: E Lai excelled at malice; the lords drew farther away.
units.literal: E Lai was skilled at slander; by this the lords grew more distant.

units.zh: 西伯歸，乃陰修德行善，諸侯多叛紂而往歸西伯。
units.en: The Western Earl went home and quietly built virtue; many lords forsook Zhou for him.
units.literal: Western Earl returning secretly cultivated virtue doing good; many lords rebelled against Zhou and went to join Western Earl.

units.zh: 西伯滋大，紂由是稍失權重。
units.en: As the Western Earl grew mighty, Zhou's grip slackened.
units.literal: Western Earl grew greater; Zhou thereby gradually lost weight of power.

units.zh: 王子比干諫，弗聽。
units.en: Prince Bigan remonstrated; Zhou would not hear him.
units.literal: Prince Bigan remonstrated; he would not listen.

units.zh: 商容賢者，百姓愛之，紂廢之。
units.en: Shang Rong was worthy and beloved; Zhou dismissed him.
units.literal: Shang Rong was a worthy; the hundred surnames loved him; Zhou cast him aside.

units.zh: 及西伯伐饑國，滅之，紂之臣祖伊聞之而咎周，恐，奔告紂曰：「天既訖我殷命，假人元龜，無敢知吉，非先王不相我後人，維王淫虐用自絕，故天棄我，不有安食，不虞知天性，不迪率典。
units.en: When the Western Earl destroyed Ji, Zuyi, a minister of Zhou, heard of it, was alarmed by the Zhou state's rise, and rushed in fear to warn King Zhou, saying, "Heaven has ended Yin's mandate; even the great tortoise cannot show good fortune. It is not that the former kings have forsaken us, but that the king's cruelty has cut us off from Heaven, so we lack peace, ignore Heaven's will, and spurn the statutes.
units.literal: When the Western Earl destroyed the state of Ji, Zuyi, a minister of Zhou, heard of it, was alarmed at the Zhou state's rise, and in fear rushed to report to King Zhou, saying, "Heaven has already ended the mandate of Yin; when we consult the great tortoise, none dare pronounce good fortune. It is not that the former kings do not aid us their descendants, but that the king by dissolute cruelty has cut himself off, so Heaven abandons us. We lack secure food, do not heed Heaven's mind, and do not follow the statutes.

units.zh: 今我民罔不欲喪，曰『天曷不降威，大命胡不至』？
units.en: Now none of your people but wishes this house to fall, crying, "When will Heaven strike—why does the great mandate not come?"
units.literal: Now none of your people but wishes this house to perish, crying, "When will Heaven send down its terrors—why does the great mandate not come?"

units.zh: 今王其柰何？」
units.en: What will you do now, my king?"
units.literal: What will you do now, my king?"

units.zh: 紂曰：「我生不有命在天乎！」
units.en: Zhou said, "Was I not born with Heaven’s mandate?"
units.literal: Zhou said, "Was I not born with a mandate from Heaven?"

units.zh: 祖伊反，曰：「紂不可諫矣。」
units.en: Zu Yi returned and said, "Zhou can no longer be remonstrated with."
units.literal: Zuyi returned and said, "Zhou cannot be admonished."

units.zh: 西伯既卒，周武王之東伐，至盟津，諸侯叛殷會周者八百。
units.en: After the Western Earl died, King Wu marched east to Mengjin; eight hundred lords who had turned from Yin rallied to him.
units.literal: Western Earl having passed away, King Wu of Zhou campaigned east, reaching Mengjin; lords rebelling against Yin who met Zhou were eight hundred.

units.zh: 諸侯皆曰：「紂可伐矣。」
units.en: The feudal lords all said, "Zhou can be attacked now."
units.literal: The lords all said, "Zhou may be attacked."

units.zh: 武王曰：「爾未知天命。」
units.en: King Wu said, "You do not yet understand Heaven’s mandate."
units.literal: King Wu said, "You do not yet know Heaven's mandate."

units.zh: 乃復歸。
units.en: So he marched home.
units.literal: Thereupon he returned.

units.zh: 紂愈淫亂不止。
units.en: Zhou sank deeper into vice without end.
units.literal: Zhou further dissolute and chaotic without stop.

units.zh: 微子數諫不聽，乃與大師、少師謀，遂去。
units.en: Weizi remonstrated repeatedly but was not heard; he then consulted with the Grand Master and Junior Master and departed.
units.literal: Weizi pleaded again and again in vain, then conspired with the grand and junior masters and left.

units.zh: 比干曰：「為人臣者，不得不以死爭。」
units.en: Bigan said, "A minister who will not risk death is no minister."
units.literal: Bigan said, "Being someone's minister, one cannot but contend with death."

units.zh: 乃彊諫紂。
units.en: He then rebuked Zhou bluntly.
units.literal: Thereupon he strongly remonstrated Zhou.

units.zh: 紂怒曰：「吾聞聖人心有七竅。」
units.en: Zhou raged, "I hear a sage's heart has seven chambers."
units.literal: Zhou angrily said, "I have heard the sage's heart has seven openings."

units.zh: 剖比干，觀其心。
units.en: He cut Bigan open to look at his heart.
units.literal: He cut open Bigan and viewed his heart.

units.zh: 箕子懼，乃詳狂為奴，紂又囚之。
units.en: Jizi feigned madness as a slave in terror; Zhou jailed him too.
units.literal: Jizi feared, then feigned madness as a slave; Zhou again imprisoned him.

units.zh: 殷之大師、少師乃持其祭樂器奔周。
units.en: The Grand Master and Junior Master of Yin then took the sacrificial and musical vessels and fled to Zhou.
units.literal: Yin's grand and junior masters fled to Zhou carrying the ritual vessels.

units.zh: 周武王於是遂率諸侯伐紂。
units.en: King Wu then led the host against Zhou.
units.literal: King Wu of Zhou thereupon then led the lords to attack Zhou.

units.zh: 紂亦發兵距之牧野。
units.en: Zhou sent an army to meet him at Muye.
units.literal: Zhou also raised troops to resist him at Muye.

units.zh: 甲子日，紂兵敗。
units.en: On the jiazi day, Zhou’s army was defeated.
units.literal: On the jiazi day, Zhou's army was defeated.

units.zh: 紂走入，登鹿臺，衣其寶玉衣，赴火而死。
units.en: Zhou fled inside, climbed the Deer Terrace, put on his robe of precious jades, and threw himself into the flames.
units.literal: Zhou fled within, climbed Lutai in his jeweled robes, and burned himself to death.

units.zh: 周武王遂斬紂頭，縣之［大］白旗。
units.en: King Wu of Zhou then cut off Zhou’s head and hung it from the great white banner.
units.literal: King Wu struck off his head and raised it on the great white standard.

units.zh: 殺妲己。
units.en: He executed Daji.
units.literal: He killed Daji.

units.zh: 釋箕子之囚，封比干之墓，表商容之閭。
units.en: He freed Jizi, sealed Bigan's grave, and honored Shang Rong's lane.
units.literal: He released Jizi from prison, sealed Bigan's tomb, marked Shang Rong's lane.

units.zh: 封紂子武庚、祿父，以續殷祀，令修行盤庚之政。
units.en: He enfeoffed Zhou's son Wugeng—Lufu—to keep Yin sacrifices and follow Pangeng's rule.
units.literal: He enfeoffed Zhou's son Wugeng, Lufu, to continue Yin sacrifices, ordering him to practice Pangeng's government.

units.zh: 殷民大說。
units.en: The Yin people rejoiced.
units.literal: Yin people greatly rejoiced.

units.zh: 於是周武王為天子。
units.en: King Wu then became Son of Heaven.
units.literal: Thereupon King Wu of Zhou became Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 其後世貶帝號，號為王。
units.en: Later Zhou dropped the title emperor and called its rulers kings.
units.literal: His later generations lowered the title emperor, styling them kings.

units.zh: 而封殷後為諸侯，屬周。
units.en: Yin's descendants were enfeoffed as lords under Zhou.
units.literal: And he enfeoffed Yin's posterity as lords, subordinate to Zhou.

units.zh: 周武王崩，武庚與管叔、蔡叔作亂，成王命周公誅之，而立微子於宋，以續殷後焉。
units.en: When King Wu died, Wugeng and the lords of Guan and Cai rebelled; King Cheng ordered the Duke of Zhou to crush them and set Weizi in Song to carry on Yin's line.
units.literal: When King Wu of Zhou died, Wugeng rebelled with the lords of Guan and Cai; King Cheng ordered the Duke of Zhou to execute them and established Weizi in Song to continue Yin's line.

units.zh: 太史公曰：余以頌次契之事，自成湯以來，采於書詩。
units.en: The Grand Historian remarks: I ordered Xie's story by the hymns; from Cheng Tang I drew on the Documents and the Odes.
units.literal: The Grand Historian says: I have arranged Xie's affairs in the order of the hymns; from Cheng Tang onward I have drawn on the Documents and the Odes.

units.zh: 契為子姓，其後分封，以國為姓，有殷氏、來氏、宋氏、空桐氏、稚氏、北殷氏、目夷氏。
units.en: Xie's house took the name Zi; later branches used their domains as surnames, yielding houses such as Yin, Lai, Song, Kongtong, Zhi, Beiyin, and Moyi.
units.literal: Xie was of the Zi surname; later enfeoffments divided, and states became surnames—there were the Yin, Lai, Song, Kongtong, Zhi, Beiyin, and Moyi clans.

units.zh: 孔子曰，殷路車為善，而色尚白。
units.en: Confucius said the Yin state carriages were the best of their day and that they favored the color white.
units.literal: Confucius said the Yin state carriages were the best of their day and they favored the color white.
